characters.description: A powerful remote mentor who advances Tala's education by sending introductory mageling, inscription, and material-reference books. His instruction gives her a foundation for understanding her unusual magic and artifacts.
characters.name: Grediv

characters.description: The name Tala gives her dimensional storage item after it repeatedly enlarges and arranges its interior for her. It remains responsive but poorly understood, needs power, and cannot yet provide a fully secure refuge.
characters.name: Kit

characters.description: The name accepted by the dimensional bird that has been following Tala. He protects her from a threatening group, can change size and scout nearby people, and responds reliably to jerky, although Tala cannot command him.
characters.name: Terry

characters.description: Trent's mageling and a returning caravan mage. Renix is ready to purchase independent inscriptions and graduate, but freely remains Trent's student while preparing to share magical responsibility on the return journey.
characters.name: Renix

characters.description: A returning caravan mage whose assignment changes before the departure from Alefast. She will not accompany Tala, Trent, and Renix on the return caravan, requiring the group to proceed without her established magical support.
characters.name: Atrexia

characters.description: A caravan military authority who interrupts Tala while she empowers the Guild's cargo slots and challenges her right to perform the work. His intervention disrupts her concentration, and the dispute remains unsettled when he first appears.
characters.name: Master sergeant

characters.description: An exceptionally large immaterial creator who joins the caravan after training under Grediv. He specializes in creating kinetic energy and appears powerful but socially inexperienced.
characters.name: Young kinetic mage

characters.description: A caravan driver who cautions Tala against reckless violence because others now depend on her. The warning emphasizes her responsibility to the people relying on her work.
characters.name: Caravan driver

characters.description: A guard and hand-to-hand instructor who begins the next stage of Tala's physical training. He assigns sustained core work and plans morning sparring against partners able to test her unusual defenses.
characters.name: Adam

characters.description: An experienced material creator assigned to caravan protection. He notices that partly eaten magical creatures may be bait left by a larger hunter and approaches potential danger with close attention to rules.
characters.name: Senior air-focused caravan mage

characters.description: A guard and former student of Adam who offers to spar with Tala.
characters.name: Ashin

characters.description: An overwhelming magic user who confronts Tala in the mountains. She recognizes the Archon Stars within Tala and offers to erase Tala's obligations and pay her heavily in return for permanent, subordinate soul-bonded service.
characters.name: Unnamed powerful mountain woman

characters.description: Tala's practical Guild contact in Bandfast. She received notice that Tala was missing, organized emergency arrangements for the affected cargo, and now explains the financial and administrative consequences of the disappearance.
characters.name: Lyn

characters.description: An inscriber in Bandfast who takes Tala directly to her workshop after the caravan returns. She is ready to begin the next stage of the defensive inscription work Tala has been awaiting and approaches the treatment as specialized professional work.
characters.name: Holly

recaps.ending: Tala and Terry reach Bandfast with the caravan. Terry's collar permits him inside the city but restricts how far he can travel from Tala, leaving their partnership workable but still dangerous and poorly understood. Lyn tells Tala that the emergency response to her disappearance has added roughly one gold ounce to her obligations and requires a senior Guild review before she accepts another contract. Holly uses an automated inscriber to rebuild Tala's arms, legs, and torso with dense, always-active defenses. Holly then reveals that she is an Archon and identifies Tala's blood-made construct as a genuine Archon Star. Tala may eventually qualify for Archon consideration, but she must first make a properly powered star and avoid all further soul bonds. Her external inscription upgrade is complete, while nightly work on her organs still awaits study. Adam's tailored combat project, Tala's family and Guild debts, whether magic wells altered Terry and the nature of his abilities, and her planned research into transferring harvested power all remain open.
recaps.in_short: Tala develops her artifacts and magic while preparing a Guild caravan for the journey from Alefast to Bandfast. Her bond with a knife deepens, her storage item becomes Kit, and the dimensional predator Terry becomes a conditional companion. After training with powerful allies, she is abducted by giant ravens and survives with Terry's help. She refuses an unknown woman's offer to clear her debts in exchange for permanent subordinate soul service, discovers that wild magic wells can permanently alter creatures, and returns to the caravan. In Bandfast, Tala faces Guild review and added costs from her disappearance. Holly rebuilds her limbs and torso with always-active inscriptions, reveals that she is an Archon, and confirms Tala's blood construct as an Archon Star. Tala ends stronger but still indebted, with internal inscription work unfinished and instructions to strengthen a star without forming more soul bonds.

recaps.text: Previously: Tala is established as a dimensional mage working with the Caravaner's Guild and developing as an immaterial guide. Trent is a trusted caravan defensive mage and adviser, while the powerful Grediv guides her development from a distance. Renix remains Trent's mageling and works within the same caravan circle. Tala also has several specialized contacts outside that mentorship: Lyn supports her Guild work, Holly handles her inscriptions, and Adam provides hand-to-hand instruction. Brand combines caravan cooking with membership in the Order of the Harvest, while Artia is another Order contact whose household deals in artifacts. Atrexia is an established caravan mage. These relationships place Tala within overlapping networks of Guild service, magical education, physical training, artifact work, and harvest expertise. She enters the new volume with professional obligations already in place and with allies able to advise her, although her unusual abilities still require further control and study.

Tala spends her remaining time near Alefast gathering ending berries and preparing cargo capacity for the Caravaner's Guild. She feeds raw power into her unusual storage item, which enlarges and organizes itself, and places blood-made Archon Stars into her artifact knife. The resulting bond lets her power and summon the knife at a distance, although the effort causes serious strain. The ending-tree grove proves hazardous even through her iron salve, but she secures a large harvest and trades some of it to Artia's household for artifact research, a magic comb, and a water-producing incorporator. Tala names the responsive storage space Kit. A dimensional bird that has been shadowing her kills a group of woodsmen who intended to exploit her, and Tala names the creature Terry. He behaves intelligently, changes size, travels through space, and protects her, but she has no dependable control over him. By the end of this stage, Tala has converted a dangerous harvest into useful knowledge and equipment while gaining two powerful, poorly understood assets in Kit and Terry.

Tala prepares to leave Alefast with Trent, Renix, and a caravan carrying twenty cargo slots under her power. She receives self-repairing travel clothes from an anonymous benefactor. Grediv examines her possessions and explains that the knife is soul-bound through an Archon Star, while Kit and her clothing are magic-bound. He warns that damage to a soul-bound object can harm her gate and that further bonding is dangerous before she becomes much stronger. Tala then helps Grediv fight an adult mountain cyclops. The creature nearly kills her and consumes all her stored ending-berry protection before Grediv destroys it. In payment, Grediv gives her a large magical library, although advanced volumes remain closed to anyone below Archon level. Kit continues adapting to Tala's needs and resists another person's attempt to open it. Adam begins her hand-to-hand training, and a young kinetic mage formerly trained by Grediv joins the caravan. Before departure, Tala concentrates her ending berries into juice, the master sergeant apologizes for challenging her cargo work, and she confirms that Terry is secretly following the caravan.

On the road, a senior air-focused mage warns that partly eaten magical creatures may signal a larger hunter near the caravan. Tala continues training with Adam and Ashin while studying how her equipment is bound. She makes a much stronger Archon Star, but the attempt drains nearly all her reserves. The young kinetic mage hunts magical bovines and arranges a vast supply of meat and jerky for her, while Adam cautions that his combat magic makes him an unsafe sparring partner until her fundamentals improve. Tala combines her tunic and trousers into one regenerating garment and tests an artifact hammer that redirects force. A full strike shatters a rock and drives fragments into her eyes, though her healing inscriptions restore her sight. Trent identifies the hammer and warns her to treat artifacts with greater care. Tala then witnesses a distant battle between four apparent human Archons and a vastly powerful nonhuman being; one human seems to die before the creature retreats. Confronted with powers far beyond her, Tala resolves to grow stronger. She also reaches an agreement with Terry: he may remain with her if he stays small near people and does not kill humans or their animals without permission.

Tala learns to extend her knife into a heated cutting form and uses the demanding transformation to train her gate. The senior air-focused mage identifies Terry as a terror-bird hatchling and helps plan a collar that can admit him safely to Bandfast. Tala's new partnership becomes known within the caravan, though Trent remains cautious. She and Grediv's former mageling repair their awkward relationship, exchange magical ideas, and spar under Adam's supervision. Tala's defenses injure his hand, convincing Adam that she needs a fighting style designed around her unusual protections. The two young mages begin a more trusting study partnership, although Grediv's former student continues avoiding his own Archon-Star work. Tala also reveals that her family imposed large debts on her and sent her into magical training to repay them, after which she ended contact with them. Terry seizes and bonds himself to a specialized growth and escort collar before Tala has finished buying it. Trent settles the dispute with the seller for four gold ounces. Soon afterward, Tala falls asleep on a wagon roof and wakes as a giant magical raven carries her toward the mountains.

Tala fights the raven carrying her and survives a devastating fall through the combined protection of her inscriptions, iron salve, and remaining ending-berry power. Stranded in snowy mountains, she kills several more giant ravens with gravity magic, her transforming knife, and the repeating hammer. Terry arrives in an enormous form and destroys the final attacker. While Tala harvests useful material from the bodies, an unnamed woman of overwhelming power confronts her. The woman recognizes Tala's Archon Stars and offers to pay her debts plus a fortune if Tala accepts a permanent soul bond as her subordinate. Tala refuses. The woman effortlessly restrains both Tala and Terry, heals Tala's injuries, and departs. Terry then carries Tala toward the caravan. Along the way, Tala discovers a hidden source of lightning power that alters nearby creatures. Eight lightning terror birds attack, but Tala and Terry defeat them together. Tala concludes that Terry holds immense internal power despite having no gate and may have gained abilities from such places. They finally catch the caravan, ending Tala's isolation but leaving the nature of the wild power sources unresolved.

Back with the caravan, Tala accepts that careless sleeping arrangements contributed to her abduction. Trent assures her that her soul-bound knife is not a phylactery, because it cannot anchor her soul after death, but he and the senior caravan mage firmly warn her against forming any more soul bonds before reaching Archon status. Trent has received guidance from Grediv for beginning his own advancement, while the senior mage finally reads a long-ignored letter from their mentor. The group explains that wild magic wells permanently grant abilities to creatures and are usually lethal to humans. Tala then creates another blood Archon Star in only an hour, evidence that surviving the mountain battles greatly increased her magical flow. The caravan reaches Bandfast with Terry admitted under the collar's distance-sensitive tether. Lyn reports that Tala's disappearance forced emergency cargo arrangements, added about one gold ounce to her costs, and requires a senior Guild meeting before she takes another contract. With the journey complete but its consequences unresolved, Holly brings Tala directly to her workshop to resume inscription work.

Holly redesigns Tala's defenses around her improved magical flow, using an automated inscriber to place dense, always-active gold workings throughout her arms, legs, and torso. Tala commits most of her available money to the treatment and endures extreme pain as the machine works through bone and soft tissue, even requiring her heart to stop briefly during the torso procedure. She emerges with stronger, continuously active defenses and regeneration, while retaining coordinated movement and gaining access to her hand-based magic through either arm. Holly then drops her concealed aura and reveals that she is an Archon. After examining Tala's blood-made construct, she confirms that it is a genuine Archon Star and accepts that Tala might eventually qualify for Archon consideration. Her advice matches the other warnings: Tala must build a properly powered star and form no additional soul bonds. The book closes with Tala at Lyn's home, physically much stronger and reunited with Terry. Her organ inscriptions remain to be completed after further study. Guild review, family and professional debts, Terry's unexplained changes, combat training, and artifact research all remain active concerns as Tala prepares for the next stage of advancement.

characters.description: A 35-year-old man from Earth who dies in a bicycle accident and accepts an offered respawn. He awakens in a younger body inside an unfamiliar character-creation room, able to understand writing he has never learned.
characters.name: Arlo

characters.description: The unidentified divine being attached to Arlo's character record. The patron appears responsible for his unusual arrival benefits and has intervened in his former life, but its identity and purpose remain unknown.
characters.name: Arlo's divine patron

characters.description: The pale, armored leader of Arlo's creation party. Varrin distrusts the poorly equipped newcomer's lack of preparation.
characters.name: Varrin

characters.description: A red-skinned cleric who is capable of fighting on the front line.
characters.name: Xim

characters.description: A low-lord archer and trained associate of Varrin in the newly formed creation party. Her ranged attacks give the group an answer to threats that Arlo cannot safely reach.
characters.name: Chilla Stormreiss

characters.description: A beast-person spear fighter and Littan Empire candidate assigned to Arlo's creation party.
characters.name: Sayil Starion

characters.description: The displaced executive core of Toxic Grotto, carried in a rune-covered orb. Hognay has coerced Grotto into drawing candidates to their deaths, making the core both a crucial guide and an ally the survivors cannot fully trust.
characters.name: Grotto

characters.description: A level-two infiltrator who coerces Grotto, stages wounds on murdered candidates, and drains Toxic Grotto through a summoned C'thun. He can impose mental commands and escapes Arlo's first attack through a shifting breach.
characters.name: Hognay

characters.description: An armed Guardian assigned to escort and monitor Arlo after officials discover that he is missing from the creation-group records. Lito watches the unregistered newcomer closely while the facility investigates his entry.
characters.name: Lito

characters.description: A gold-level official who retrieves Arlo's Delver record and accepts its redacted nationality as enough to clear the immediate records dispute. Grotto quietly suppresses the unusual emotional effect her presence has on Arlo.
characters.name: Myria

characters.description: A powerful Third Layer traveler who welcomes Arlo at a family dinner and begins the process of admitting him to the tribe. He also accepts Grotto, recognizing that the core and Arlo are bound together.
characters.name: Drel'Gethed

characters.description: The new permanent name of the Earth-born Delver after his adoption into a Third Layer tribe. Xim sponsors him, Drel'Gethed conducts the rite, and Grotto is admitted alongside him, giving Arlo a recognized community and identity.
characters.name: Arlo Xor'Drel

characters.description: A senior member of the Ravvenblaq family who meets Arlo alongside his wife and thanks him for saving Varrin.
characters.name: Ealdric

characters.description: A platinum-level Eschendur captive found beside Xim beneath the warehouse. Nuralie has scales, a tail, and practical skill with alchemy and medicine, using an improvised stimulant to revive Xim after their captor withdraws.
characters.name: Nuralie

characters.description: An immense cave-dwelling entity whose soul overwhelms Arlo's perception. Orexis absorbs fallen Delvers and claims that the rebels acted under the influence of its desires before seizing Varrin.
characters.name: Orexis

characters.description: An overwhelming divine attacker who defeats high-level Delvers with speed, multiple limbs, shielding, and varied magic, then forces the survivors into the inactive Calvani Caverns.
characters.name: Divine captor

characters.description: Orexis's sister and an imprisoned divine avatar embodying release. Fortune removes Anesis from Cage through the portal network and takes her to Hiward, leaving Orexis's soul fragment behind.
characters.name: Anesis

characters.description: A six-armed clay figure animated through a primordial obelisk to complete the captor's forced five-person Cage team. The construct is intended to hold part of its creator's soul, but Grotto interrupts the procedure before stabilization is complete.
characters.name: Clay construct

characters.description: The name chosen by the clay construct after Cage runes expel the possessing soul fragment. Etja says her original imposed purpose ended with that separation, and Arlo prevents her execution while the party assesses her independent will.
characters.name: Etja

characters.description: The core of a containment Delve destabilized by a Void Sphere. Cage assigns the trapped team to prevent collapse and stop a divine specter from breaching central confinement.
characters.name: Cage

characters.description: A captive divine aspect that Cage considers the safest available countermeasure. Freeing Fortune may stop the specter, or Anesis if needed, though the party remains wary of every prisoner in the failing Delve.
characters.name: Fortune

characters.description: Fortune is the divine being responsible for Arlo's arrival. He confirms that he transported the continuous Arlo from Earth and that the world Arlo left is now millennia beyond recovery.
characters.name: Fortune

characters.description: A powerful extradimensional creature summoned by Arlo during the battle for Cage's first lock. Shog Tuatha protects Etja, opposes the swarming aberrations, and remains bound to Arlo for the spell's duration.
characters.name: Shog Tuatha

characters.description: A Ravvenblaq family elder who meets Arlo with Ealdric and thanks him for saving Varrin.
characters.name: Ravvenblaq matriarch

characters.description: A Ravvenblaq family elder who joins the expedition investigating Calvani Caverns and the attack on the family's lands.
characters.name: Ravvenblaq patriarch

recaps.ending: Arlo, Grotto, Xim, Varrin, Nuralie, and Etja escape Cage alive after destroying Orexis's remaining specter and preventing the Delve's immediate collapse. Ealdric is dead, while Lito and Drel'Gethed survived their initial injuries outside Cage. The Void Sphere is removed from Hiward's Reality Anchor and now rests in stasis within Arlo's quick-access inventory, but no permanent disposal method is known. Grotto channels the sphere's mana through the pocket Delve, expands it, and gives Xim, Varrin, Nuralie, and Etja Rebirth mana veins, repairing their urgent damage. Etja is accepted as a full party member. The group chooses Soulsbane as its name, but the system registers Arlo as leader of Fortune's Folly instead. Fortune has taken Anesis to Hiward, where she escapes after fighting Myria and the Ravvenblaq matriarch. The surviving party therefore faces an at-large divine enemy, uncertainty over Fortune's aims, possible Crown claims against the pocket Delve, and the continuing danger of the stored sphere.
recaps.in_short: After dying on Earth, Arlo respawns in a system-governed world and survives a sabotaged creation Delve with Varrin and Xim. He bonds its displaced core, Grotto, joins a Third Layer tribe as Arlo Xor'Drel, and builds a pocket Delve inside his inventory. An attempted abduction leads him, Xim, Varrin, Nuralie, and their allies to Calvani Caverns, where divine forces coerce them into the failing containment Delve called Cage. The construct Etja is freed from possession and joins them. Fortune reveals that he brought Arlo from an Earth now millennia beyond recovery, then removes Anesis to Hiward and leaves the party to fight Orexis's soul fragment. Varrin destroys the fragment after Arlo shares its vulnerability. The group removes a destabilizing Void Sphere, uses its mana to repair their damaged mana veins, and escapes. Anesis remains at large, the sphere remains in Arlo's inventory, and the system names Arlo's party Fortune's Folly despite their choice of Soulsbane.

recaps.text:
Arlo dies when a car strikes his bicycle, then accepts an interface offer to respawn in a new zone. Character creation restores him to a younger body and grants unusual options linked to an unidentified divine patron. He selects the Traveler birth sign, a healing ring, dimensional magic, a short-range teleport called Shortcut, a touch attack, and an aura that shares his strong health regeneration with allies. He conceals his outsider origin after joining Varrin, Xim, Chilla Stormreiss, and Sayil Starion in a creation party.

Varrin asserts leadership through noble rank and selects Platinum difficulty without group approval. The party enters Toxic Grotto, where poisonous fog and venomous creatures make Arlo's regeneration central to survival. His lack of combat experience is clear, but he learns to use his magic under pressure and protects Xim during an ambush. After the group crosses a crumbling bridge, an atrocodile drags Varrin into the river. The party kills it, but the creature's fear effect has scattered them. They then find Chilla dead in a side passage, leaving the survivors trapped in a lethal Delve with an unknown additional threat.

The survivors discover that Toxic Grotto contains an automated poison-essence farm far beyond what they expected from a creation Delve. During another ambush, Sayil vanishes and dies without an evident struggle. Arlo, Varrin, and Xim find his mutilated body and evidence that someone has been stripping essence from the facility. In the lower tunnels, a mental command draws Arlo toward Hognay, an infiltrator carrying the displaced Delve Core. Arlo resists, wounds him, and takes the orb.

The core, named Grotto by the party, admits that Hognay coerced it into arranging Chilla's and Sayil's deaths. Hognay has damaged the obelisk and summoned a C'thun to drain the Delve. The survivors attempt to restore Grotto while fighting both enemies. Arlo apparently kills Hognay, but the C'thun breaks the obelisk and nearly overwhelms everyone. Arlo bonds Grotto as his familiar, allowing the core to absorb his mana overload and guide a final attack. Arlo reshapes his dimensional spell into a beam and kills the C'thun. He confirms Hognay's death, and Arlo, Xim, Varrin, and Grotto leave the ruined Delve alive.

At the post-Delve facility, healers treat Xim and Varrin while officials question why Arlo was absent from the participant records. Guardian Lito escorts him under suspicion. Grotto now shares sensation and thought with Arlo, and their bond greatly increases his mana recovery. Arlo also discovers that his dimensional magic can evolve into an expandable pocket space, which Grotto believes could house a new Delve.

Myria retrieves a valid record showing that Arlo entered as a last-minute replacement, though his nationality is redacted. Once the immediate dispute is cleared, Arlo tells Xim and Varrin about his death, character creation, and origin in a world without magic. They recognize that his ability to train attributes beyond normal limits makes him both powerful and vulnerable to exploitation. Varrin offers a path to Hiwardian protection through his family, while Xim offers membership in her Third Layer tribe. Arlo chooses the tribal route. Drel'Gethed accepts both him and Grotto, and Xim sponsors the adoption. The rite gives him the permanent name Arlo Xor'Drel, a recognized Third Layer identity, new resistances, and additional magic.

Arlo settles in Foundation while Xim completes required devotions. He opens his expanded pocket space and authorizes Grotto to establish a Delve within it, retaining authority over its limits. Study and training rapidly raise Arlo's attributes, and Grotto completes an obelisk that makes the pocket Delve operational. Soon afterward, a hired Delver party invades Arlo's home to abduct him. The pocket defenses help him kill three attackers and capture two.

Lito and Myria investigate. The prisoners connect the job to an information broker and to the Ring of Calvani, which grants entry to Calvani Caverns and offers an illicit route to becoming a Delver. Tracking the ring leads to a low-lord crime boss, but the confrontation becomes a battle when Arlo senses Xim imprisoned beneath the warehouse. He finds Xim and Nuralie held by a Littan controller, who departs rather than fight. Nuralie revives Xim and helps defeat the crime boss upstairs.

Central authorizes an expedition to Calvani Caverns. Arlo enlarges the pocket dimension to support the travelers, obtains armor and weapons, gains physical magic, and trains with a warhammer. During the river journey, a wounded winged resident warns that a hostile flock has attacked a colony and targeted ships bound for Arsenal. The expedition defeats the attackers and rescues surviving children and captives, but their sponsor and connection to the wider trade disruption remain uncertain.

Lito continues Arlo's hammer instruction, while Grotto studies the unusual mana structure that permits Arlo's training gains and considers whether it could eventually help his companions. Arlo reaches key physical milestones, learns to carry his dimensional attack through a weapon, and becomes co-administrator of the pocket Delve. The expedition reaches the mountain rendezvous and prepares for the approach to Calvani Caverns, still uncertain about the force behind the abductions and attacks.

Varrin joins Arlo, Xim, and Nuralie in a formal party, with Arlo chosen as leader. The larger expedition approaches Calvani Caverns through the dangerous Third Layer after Drel'Gethed detects scouts and a divine mana event. A vast eye notices Arlo during the crossing, and he senses an overwhelming void-like presence at their destination. Back in ordinary reality, the group defeats hostile Delvers, but Orexis emerges, absorbs the dead, and claims that its desires drove the rebellion.

The divine confrontation overwhelms the expedition. The survivors are forced into Calvani Caverns, where their captor opens Cage, a failing containment Delve destabilized by a Void Sphere. Ealdric is killed to power a primordial creation obelisk, and a clay construct is made as a fifth team member and intended soul vessel. Grotto sabotages the procedure, but the construct carries Arlo, Xim, Varrin, and Nuralie through the portal. Cage's runes expel the possessing fragment, and the construct names herself Etja. Arlo spares her as an autonomous being. Cage then charges the five-person party with preventing collapse and stopping a divine specter from breaching central confinement.

Cage explains that the Void Sphere is destabilizing a Hiward reality anchor and waking imprisoned divine beings. Unable to release prisoners directly, Cage asks the party to open two locks and awaken Fortune as a defense against the specter. Arlo summons Shog Tuatha during the first lock battle, and Etja proves herself as a powerful combat caster. At the second lock, the group defeats a coordinated hive of eyes, hands, and a corrosive plant, then enters central confinement.

The party awakens Fortune, who confirms that he transported the same continuous Arlo from Earth. Earth is now thousands of years beyond Arlo's former life, leaving no path back to his family. Fortune admits that Arlo's arrival was meant to facilitate his release. He agrees to confront Anesis but refuses to protect the party from Orexis. Nuralie, Xim, and Arlo use a piece of Fortune's soul to craft arrows capable of poisoning Orexis's incorporeal fragment.

Orexis's soul fragment attacks after Fortune removes Anesis to Hiward. It identifies Etja as its created daughter, wounds Arlo, suppresses his casting, and nearly consumes Shog Tuatha. Arlo discovers Reveal, an ability that shares his soul perception with his companions. Through it, the party sees that the fragment is unstable and vulnerable. Nuralie's divine arrows weaken it, Xim returns in an Ascended form, and Grotto forces it to confront its incomplete nature. Varrin's Soul Strike splits and destroys the fragment.

The wounded party still must prevent Cage from collapsing. Etja removes the Void Sphere from Hiward's Reality Anchor but suffers severe mana-vein damage. Grotto channels the sphere's output into the pocket Delve, expanding it and using knowledge from Calvani Caverns to give Xim, Varrin, Nuralie, and Etja Rebirth mana veins. Their urgent damage is repaired, and Xim can cleanse her remaining lethal afflictions. Arlo then stores the still-dangerous sphere in inventory stasis. Everyone exits alive, and Etja becomes a full member. Anesis has escaped after fighting Myria and the Ravvenblaq matriarch. The group chooses Soulsbane, but the system names Arlo's party Fortune's Folly instead.

characters.description: The leader of Fortune's Folly is an exceptionally durable dimensional mage and protector. His abilities include Soul Sight, Reveal, teleportation, defensive auras, and access to a pocket Delve shared with Grotto. He is bonded to both Grotto and the wider dangers surrounding the system.
characters.name: Arlo Xor'Drel

characters.description: A Delve Core bonded to Arlo and resident in their shared pocket Delve. Grotto can speak into Arlo's mind, manifest a physical form, and alter the Delve under his control.
characters.name: Grotto

characters.description: A cleric and frontline fighter in Arlo's party. Xim combines healing, shields, and divine fire with an ascended bestial combat form.
characters.name: Xim

characters.description: A Ravvenblaq swordsman who serves as one of the party's principal frontline fighters. Varrin is a politically connected Delver whose family carries knowledge and obligations concerning Hiward.
characters.name: Varrin

characters.description: An Eschendur native who serves the party as an alchemist, archer, and scout. Nuralie seeks enough strength to return home and protect it.
characters.name: Nuralie

characters.description: A divine-made clay construct who became a Delver and developed a humanlike form. Etja uses force magic, mana shaping, Nullify, and Shared Vessel. Her inherited memories and the abilities built into her origin remain closely connected to Orexis.
characters.name: Etja

characters.description: Arlo's resilient extradimensional summon and a recurring combat ally. Shog Tuatha recovers and changes while in its home dimension.
characters.name: Shog Tuatha

characters.description: A dangerous but apparently helpful power linked to Arlo's unusual eye-derived abilities and his Traveler's Amulet. Fortune's gifts have aided Arlo, but the nature and intentions behind that aid remain uncertain.
characters.name: Fortune

characters.description: A hostile divine influence connected to Etja's creation and to the party's continuing fears. A fragment of Orexis's soul was once hidden within Etja, leaving the entity central to her history and to the group's concern about powers operating beyond ordinary Delvers.
characters.name: Orexis

characters.description: Xim's father and an elder of her Third Layer community.
characters.name: Drel'Gethed

characters.description: A level-10, system-aware Architect whose body encompasses the lesser mimics throughout its Delve. Ancient, intelligent, and recently awakened, it recognizes unusual qualities in Arlo's party but initially refuses to explain the card or the system's phased rollout.
characters.name: Mimic Architect

characters.description: A gold-level Littan Delver sent by a duchess to investigate a Littan party member's death. He questions Arlo about Varrin's involvement and appears able to judge whether the answers are truthful.
characters.name: Littan investigator

characters.description: The Littan investigator's gold-level associate. He uses shadow magic to distract or conceal Arlo's companions and can dispel Xim's flames.
characters.name: Littan shadow associate

characters.description: Xim's mother and a member of her Third Layer tribal community.
characters.name: Xim's mother

characters.description: Xim's divine mother figure and the goddess of her Third Layer tribe. She receives Arlo in her sanctuary and counsels him about his unusual gifts, avatars, and advancement through the system.
characters.name: Xim's goddess

characters.description: A level-23 Delver of Xim's tribe who practices dream forging. She agrees to assess Arlo's need for a replacement weapon.
characters.name: Tribal dream forger

characters.description: Varrin's grandfather and the patriarch of House Ravvenblaq. A level-56 Delver, he brings Fortune's Folly into his family's response to the growing avatar crisis and warns them that their connection to an earlier avatar incident will affect Hiward's public policy.
characters.name: Ealdric Ravvenblaq Sr.

characters.description: Varrin's older brother and a Delver in another Ravvenblaq party. Ealdric Ravvenblaq IV is commonly called Drift by his companions. His usual combat work emphasizes control magic, while his family position makes him part of the political response to the avatar threat.
characters.name: Ealdric Ravvenblaq IV

characters.description: The official leading Central briefs the party on the three known special Delves and identifies the two lower-level sites as possible routes toward Phase 2. Central will not formally support the effort because wider Delver creation could conflict with Hiward's interests, but the director promises limited diplomatic help with passage through the Littan blockade.
characters.name: Director of Central

characters.description: The Littan naval commander responsible for enforcing the blockade of Eschendur. He rejects the party's newly issued passage documents, demands the surrender of Nuralie, and orders Fortune's Folly detained even though the stated grounds conflict with their valid authorization.
characters.name: Littan admiral

characters.description: The admiral commanding the Littan blockade force. Richton underestimates the threat posed by Fortune's Folly and continues to dispute the party's valid authorization. He orders a temporary fallback and rescue operation after losing four ships.
characters.name: Admiral Richton

characters.description: A level-17 imperial naval Delver commanding concealed experimental caravels. He attacks both Fortune's Folly and Littan personnel and tries to frame Arlo's group. His specialized movement effects and advanced weapons make him the central threat in the sea battle.
characters.name: Littan gold captain

characters.description: An Eschendur ruler and a religious authority associated with the water deity. The Zenithar recognizes the party's lawful passage, grants them asylum, and rejects the Littan blockade commander's attempt to seize them within Eschendur's waters.
characters.name: Zenithar of the water deity

characters.description: A level-15, platinum-ranked Dajinin Zenithar who arrives through Arlo's portal after the evacuation of Nuralie's village. Her soul appears stronger than that of the Zenithar the party previously met.
characters.name: Dajinin Zenithar

characters.description: A level-24 Architect that overwhelms nearby Littan Delvers, notices Fortune's Folly, and seizes Arlo by the throat.
characters.name: the Operator

recaps.ending: Fortune's Folly survives the remedial sequence, reaches Delver Level 10, and kills the enormous corrupted Delve remnant through a combined strategy of bleeding, divine fire, layered poisons, Shog Tuatha's rescue work, and an Explosion amplified by Etja and Arlo through Shared Vessel. The obelisk identifies the remnant as a portal guardian rather than the destination itself. Arlo, Grotto, Xim, Varrin, Nuralie, Etja, and Shog Tuatha all survive. Grotto is unsettled by the three-way combat link he mediated with Arlo and the summon, while Shog Tuatha recognizes a new concern for Xim. Nuralie takes custody of an ominous grimoire, and Arlo's evolved amulet promises eventual intrinsic-skill sharing with Grotto while implying communication from an avatar. After receiving diamond chips and major intrinsic progress, Arlo reaches Fortitude 40 and Wisdom 40. The entire party immediately crosses into another special-grade Delve with an Escape objective. Phase 2 remains locked, the Littan invasion of Eschendur continues, and neither the avatar cycle nor the Operator's history has been confirmed.
recaps.in_short: A year after the Cage, Fortune's Folly learns that the Get Out of Cage Free card points toward Phase 2 of the system and a set of special Delves. Warnings from Xim's goddess, Hiward, and the Operator establish avatars as a growing threat, though the Operator's account of repeated civilization-ending ascensions remains unverified. The party fights through the Littan blockade, kills a rogue gold captain, gains asylum in Eschendur, and becomes caught in the Littan invasion while Nuralie accepts appointment as an Inquisitor and evacuates her village. With the Operator's diversion, they enter a Littan-held special Delve, train from Level 6 to Level 10, and defeat its tailored remedial encounters. Their final opponent is a mountain-sized corrupted Delve remnant, killed through coordinated fire, bleeding, poison, and a massive Shared Vessel Explosion. The remnant proves to be a portal guardian. The surviving party takes its rewards and enters the next special-grade Delve, where the stated objective is Escape.

recaps.text: Previously: Arlo Xor'Drel leads Fortune's Folly with Xim, Varrin, Nuralie, Etja, and his bonded Delve Core, Grotto. Arlo is a highly durable dimensional mage whose abilities include Soul Sight, Reveal, teleportation, protective auras, and access to a pocket Delve. Etja was transformed from a clay construct into a Delver after carrying a fragment of Orexis, a hostile avatar-linked entity. Nuralie hopes to gain enough power to return to Eschendur and defend it. Arlo also carries unusual gifts associated with Fortune, including powers derived from his eye and an evolving Traveler's Amulet. The group survived the Cage and obtained a one-use Get Out of Cage Free card whose reference to the system's rollout remains unexplained.

Fortune's Folly clears a platinum Delve filled by one distributed mimic. The entity presents itself as the Mimic Architect, an ancient level-10 intelligence with system access and a body encompassing every lesser mimic in the site. After the party defeats its combat form, Nuralie's charged attack prevents its scattered pieces from recovering. The dying Architect examines the Get Out of Cage Free card and says it signals a cascading failure involving avatars and the system's phased rollout. Phase 1 challenges civilization, while Phase 2 would provide further resources and power after enough Delvers succeed. The party is too low-level to reach every required system core, but the Architect supplies the locations of three special Delves, including a restricted site in Eschendur. The group leaves with those leads, new loot, and another level, while postponing its decision until everyone has rested.

Arlo discovers that personally meaningful restrictions can strengthen magic and selects a Fortitude evolution that prevents bleeding and permits regeneration from any nonfatal injury. After the party compares new abilities and reasons for Delving, Varrin says that duty binds him to Hiward and Ravvenblaq, but revenge against Orexis drives him personally. Arlo warns that imperial expansion, defense treaties, unequal Delver access, and powerful weapons could lead to a multinational war. A gold-level Littan investigator then attacks him to measure his strength. Arlo survives by moving the fight into the pocket Delve and using Grotto's defenses and Shog Tuatha's help, but the attacker and a shadow-using associate escape. The assault reveals gaps in Arlo's individual offense and raises concern when Xim's divine fire reacts strangely to the associate. Varrin stays behind to investigate the Littans, while Arlo, Xim, and Grotto decide to travel to Xim's Third Layer community. Grotto admits that the phase rollout may threaten his existence, and Arlo promises that they will face that danger together.

In the Third Layer, Drel'Gethed explains how identity can reshape a manifested body, and Grotto experiments with his own form. Xim's goddess tells Arlo that avatars emerge after Delvers rise, grow stronger over time, and have destroyed earlier civilizations. She presents advancement through later system phases as a possible path to true divinity and resistance, while warning that the avatar linked to Ravvenblaq is especially dangerous. Arlo and Xim learn that only platinum-grade Delvers remain eligible for later advancement, excluding Xim's parents. During three months of training, Arlo develops his weapon skills and receives a changing warhammer forged through a communal dream. The party then reunites at Foundation after an avatar attack leaves a Timagrin city lethally saturated with mana. Ealdric Ravvenblaq Sr. says Hiward will announce an avatar kill-on-sight policy. Central quietly confirms that two lower-level special Delves may be the only available path toward Phase 2 and helps the party seek passage to Eschendur without formally endorsing the mission.

The Littan blockade refuses Fortune's Folly's valid passage, demands Nuralie's surrender, and opens a naval confrontation. A rogue level-17 Littan captain then attacks from experimental hidden caravels, killing his own side while attempting to blame Arlo's party. The fighting leaves Varrin disabled and drives Arlo through severe wounds, including a bolt through his heart. Varrin intervenes before the captain can finish Arlo, but the captain uses a deific skill to isolate Arlo in another layer until one of them dies. Arlo recovers, prepares traps and poison, summons Shog Tuatha, and kills the captain. Back in the main battle, Fortune's Folly reaches Eschendur's waters and receives asylum from the Zenithar of the water deity. When the Littan admiral continues the attack despite her ruling, the Zenithar uses overwhelming water power to destroy more than half of the blockade fleet. The surviving Littan ships retreat, and the party enters Eschendur under the Triarch's protection.

The Zenithar offers Nuralie appointment as an Inquisitor, a neutral crisis authority that would let her escort Fortune's Folly across Eschendur. As the party travels inland, it supplies a village suffering from blockade-driven shortages and treats its sick residents. Arlo works to deepen Soul Sight and Reveal, while Grotto seeks practical skills beyond his original Delve Core functions. News then arrives that a Littan legion has crossed into Eschendur through the Eshin Gap. With her home village near the invasion route, Nuralie accepts the Inquisitor office. Arlo establishes a portal destination near the capital so the group can evacuate the village if needed, and the party turns toward the threatened settlement. Eschendur mobilizes for war, while Nuralie's new authority makes the special-Delve mission inseparable from the immediate defense of her homeland.

Littan Delvers ambush the party during its approach to Nuralie's village, destroying Arlo's eye and part of his brain. He survives, expands Soul Sight to locate concealed attackers, and forges Reckless Shortcut, a long-range teleport that severely injures him when used. The party defeats the ambushers, evacuates more than a hundred villagers through Arlo's portal, and learns that the occupiers killed the local defenders. A Dajinin Zenithar takes custody of a prisoner but cannot abandon the invasion response to join the larger mission. Near the local special Delve, Fortune's Folly meets the Operator, a level-24 Architect protecting the site's reality anchor. The Operator recognizes Grotto as Core 1156 and finds his bond with Arlo anomalous. It claims that flawed ascensions created avatars and that successive civilizations have repeated the catastrophe more quickly. It also warns that Phase 2 would strengthen avatars as well as Delvers. The party treats this history as unverified but chooses advancement as its best available defense. The Operator agrees to distract the Littan force guarding the Delve.

The Operator engages the Littan base's strongest defender while Fortune's Folly uses Nuralie's diversions, Etja's ward-breaking, Xim's fear effect, and Varrin's soul-disrupting sword technique to reach the portal. Once inside, the party endures the attention of multiple divine beings and learns that the special Delve judges every member underprepared. It grants access to an immense training facility but imposes a 30-day deadline to reach Delver Level 10. Nuralie becomes an Inquisitor in class as well as office and recognizes Eschendur's three gods as aspects of a greater whole. An outside force replaces all of Arlo's Luck evolutions with a dangerous offer to invoke a divine being's true name, so he defers the choice. The party trains intensively, and Arlo forges powerful self-repairing heavy armor. After entering the remedial portal, Shog Tuatha kills the first guardian and begins another advance. The victory awards progress and stat points, but the chamber immediately collapses into the next trial.

The next trial is an escalating clockwork chamber that attacks the party with weight, heat, lightning, mental pressure, and restraints. Xim sustains the group while Arlo exposes the mechanism's hidden soul and Varrin destroys its core, earning a powerful shield for Xim. A crystal entity then isolates the companions in tailored encounters. Each wins independently, and Nuralie identifies the need for simultaneous attacks on the central crystal. After that victory, Etja incorporates the Prismatic Mask and gains line-spell effects, while Etja, Nuralie, and Varrin receive major attribute evolutions. The floor then gives way beneath the party, dropping everyone through a stormy sky toward the mountain-sized Delve remnant. Fortune's Folly enters the new encounter with stronger abilities but without a safe interval to recover fully.

Fortune's Folly attacks the Delve remnant through accumulating damage rather than direct penetration. Varrin opens bleeding wounds, Xim spreads divine fire, and Nuralie layers many poisons so their combined toxicity can grow. Etja and Arlo use Shared Vessel to shape and amplify a massive Explosion inside the remnant's eye, drawing its attention away from the others. When Arlo is nearly killed, Shog Tuatha rescues him and Grotto mediates a three-way mental link that lets Arlo guide the summon through Soul Sight and Reveal. The linked group also recovers Xim and the unconscious Varrin. Nuralie doubles the remnant's toxicity, and the accumulated wounds finally kill it. The obelisk reveals that this enemy was a portal guardian and awards diamond chips plus major intrinsic progress. Arlo reaches Fortitude 40 and Wisdom 40. His evolved amulet promises eventual sharing of intrinsic skills with Grotto and appears to carry an avatar's message. The surviving party immediately enters the next special-grade Delve, whose objective is Escape.

characters.description: The leader of Fortune's Folly and master of the Pocket Delve. Arlo is a Level 10 dimensional mage whose teleportation, Soul Sight, protective auras, and bond with Grotto make him both a front-line combatant and the center of the party's support network.
characters.name: Arlo Xor'Drel

characters.description: The Core of the Pocket Delve and Arlo's soul-linked co-operator. Grotto can manifest, communicate mentally, administer his Delve, and assist Arlo's abilities. Their unusually close connection gives each of them insight into the other's condition.
characters.name: Grotto

characters.description: A politically connected Ravvenblaq swordsman and Fortune's Folly's front-line fighter. Varrin combines disciplined weapon work with an evolving spirit whose power and instability make it a significant concern for both him and the party.
characters.name: Varrin

characters.description: A divine fighter and healer in Fortune's Folly. Xim fights at close range with divine fire, shields, fear effects, and a formidable transformation, while her healing and defensive magic allow the party to survive otherwise fatal engagements.
characters.name: Xim

characters.description: A displaced Eschendur native who serves as an Inquisitor, scout, alchemist, and archer. Nuralie specializes in poisons, traps, precise ranged attacks, detection, and spiritual investigation, giving the party both battlefield control and careful analysis.
characters.name: Nuralie

characters.description: A sentient construct-bodied Delver with inherited memories and potent divine magic. Etja can use Nullify and Shared Vessel, but her origin includes a harmful connection to Orexis that remains a danger rather than an allegiance.
characters.name: Etja

characters.description: Arlo's resilient extradimensional combat summon. He can recover in his home dimension and return changed by his experiences, making him a powerful but independently minded ally whose physical, dimensional, and spiritual abilities continue to develop.
characters.name: Arlo's C'than summon

characters.description: A dangerous but apparently helpful avatar-linked power associated with Arlo's unusual eye-derived abilities and Traveler's Amulet. Fortune's interest has benefited Arlo, but the extent and purpose of that influence remain uncertain.
characters.name: Fortune

characters.description: A hostile divine influence tied to Etja's origin. A shard of Orexis's soul was concealed within her, leaving the party alert to the possibility that this connection may still threaten Etja or those around her.
characters.name: Orexis

characters.description: The powerful host of the special Delve's central chamber. Avarice receives Fortune's Folly amid the doomed aspirants after Varrin recovers from the final test. Her position suggests control over this stage, but her purpose and terms have not yet been explained.
characters.name: Avarice

characters.description: A goddess invoked by a visiting spatial mage in Arlo's Expansion Delve. She offers Arlo a choice and, under the terms he accepts, tames the dimensional plant while preserving the visitors' earned rewards.
characters.name: Yara

characters.description: Varrin's younger sister and an apprentice to House Ravvenblaq's Keeper of Decorum. She arrives at Arlo's estate while preparations are underway for a royal visit.
characters.name: Riona Ravvenblaq

characters.description: One of Eschendur's three theocratic rulers. The Triarch arrives at Arlo's domain before the Hiwardian delegation and offers sovereign recognition and potential treaties if Arlo creates a governing structure for his dimensional territory.
characters.name: Eschendur Triarch

characters.description: Hiward's ruler, a first-generation Delver and former leader of a slave rebellion with thirty platinum levels. He visits Arlo's Pocket Delve to assess the rapidly advancing party and the wider avatar crisis under carefully negotiated security limits.
characters.name: Hiwardian king

characters.description: Varrin's father and a senior Ravvenblaq Delver responding to the crisis at Arlo's estate. When the guarded lounge is found empty, Ealdric tests the apparent Kingsguard, immediately recognizes the detail as false, and acts with decisive force.
characters.name: Ealdric Ravvenblaq Sr.

characters.description: A hostile avatar who confronts Arlo in a Kingsguard disguise and admits abducting the king, Fortune's Folly, and other delegates. Hysteria uses illusion, mental attacks, elaborate deception, and identity-related threats.
characters.name: Hysteria

characters.description: A power Arlo invokes inside Hysteria's isolated void prison after Varrin's sister remains unable to join the group needed for escape.
characters.name: Dread Star

characters.description: A durable divine attacker in the five-person force assaulting Arlo's mansion. The paladin engages Arlo directly while supporting the other Wastelanders with healing and consecration, revealing a more versatile combat role than a simple front-line bruiser.
characters.name: Wasteland paladin

characters.description: A member of the five-person Wasteland assault force who attacks Xim at close range during the mansion battle.
characters.name: Wasteland martial fighter

recaps.text:
Previously: Arlo Xor'Drel leads Fortune's Folly, a Level 10 Delver party whose unusual abilities draw attention from political, divine, and System powers. His dimensional magic, Soul Sight, and protective auras are strengthened by his bond with Grotto, the soul-linked Core of Arlo's Pocket Delve. Varrin is a Ravvenblaq swordsman with a dangerous evolving spirit. Xim combines divine fire, fear, shielding, and healing. Nuralie is an Eschendur Inquisitor, alchemist, scout, and poison archer. Etja is a sentient construct-bodied Delver whose origin is bound to the hostile influence Orexis. Arlo can also call a powerful C'than summon. Together, their specialized abilities let them confront challenges well beyond the reach of an ordinary party at their level.

Fortune remains an apparently helpful but uncertain patron behind some of Arlo's gifts. The party enters this volume already committed to a special Delve, carrying a single-use escape card and facing threats whose connection to avatars and the wider System is not yet understood.

Fortune's Folly remains inside the Phase 2 Delve and chooses to pursue its escape objective rather than spend its single-use escape card. After selecting new evolutions, the party crosses a long maze whose hazards include vacuum, extreme temperatures, poison, antimagic, and a creation-myth puzzle. Three attunement doors divide the group, leaving Arlo and Nuralie alone.

Their route loops between a sacred basilica and a profane cathedral that occupy the same apparent location. Each contains a button linked to buried beings, but ordinary movement cannot bridge the two sites. Arlo determines that the churches are separated along an additional spatial direction and learns to cross it with Reckless Shortcut while Nuralie follows the spiritual connection between the buttons. Their synchronized activation overlays both sites, awakens hundreds of husks, and allows a construct-icon to transfer waiting souls into living bodies. Arlo and Nuralie receive rings that extend teleportation and sensory range, then are sent to another isolated chamber as hostile insects emerge from its walls. They have solved the church trial but remain separated from their allies, and the Delve's worsening time dilation makes delay increasingly costly.

Arlo and Nuralie are forced to defend their chamber against escalating camps of insectoid doomed aspirants. The first attacker speaks, fights with trained skill, and carries a Hiwardian heirloom, raising the possibility that the aspirants are transformed or copied Delvers. The pair fortify the room with traps and kill zones, but each new wave is larger and arrives after a shorter interval.

A coordinated fourth camp nearly overwhelms them. Xim and Grotto break into the fight, and Grotto temporarily fuses his control with Arlo so they can combine movement, defense, and shared intrinsics. They defeat the camp, though Arlo is severely injured. Varrin, Etja, and Arlo's C'than summon then return from their own prolonged battle through a divine insect hive, reuniting the party before the next challenge.

The group quarantines a soul-threatening wand and learns that at least one doomed aspirant resembles a Delver missing for roughly twenty years. Evidence from the hive suggests a divine power may be corrupting the Delve, but the theory remains unconfirmed. With no visible exit, Fortune's Folly decides to investigate far enough to test that possibility instead of assuming it is true.

The reunited party crosses the artificial moon and reaches a final test requiring one soul to occupy two chambers. Varrin divides his evolving spirit without using the offered lethal axe. The separated part returns, leaving him alive but spiritually injured, and the solution opens the Delve's center.

There the party meets Avarice, whose presence initially mesmerizes most of them. After Etja exposes the influence, Avarice suppresses it and proposes an exchange of personal information and future services. She describes a mortal leader shaped by Dava's history of Delver conquest and civil war. He gained power by consuming mana-infused creatures and then merging with consenting dying people, retaining their memories. Avarice warns that he could become far more dangerous by reclaiming a released consumption avatar and using six focal sites to restore Unity.

Fortune's Folly trades information and questions to a higher power for optimized attributes, future services, and possible allies. The party learns that one Unity focal point may already be active in Timagrin. System diagnostics then show Core 1 operating at only a fraction of capacity while imitating other cores. A reboot is overridden, and a replacement personality initiates System Phase II.

System Phase II publicly names Fortune's Folly among the first escalated Delvers and opens Expansion Delves, Labyrinths, Raids, overworld dungeons, and new Creation Delves. Avarice departs after the completed bargain. The party receives new skill capacity, and Arlo develops stronger aura support, spell redirection, speed, and countermagic.

System Core 2 confirms that Grotto is both Arlo's familiar and the Core of the Pocket Delve. His familiar status allows greater openness with the party, while his Core restrictions still apply inside the Delve. When the group finally exits the special challenge, it earns an A-grade assessment and discovers that a full year has passed outside.

They emerge in a Littan fortress, but the soldiers offer diplomacy instead of arrest. An armistice with Eschendur is in force, and Nuralie accepts a letter intended for its rulers. The party delays a proposed meeting with Littan leaders for one week and retreats to the Pocket Delve. Arlo releases his Grade 18 C'than summon to tend his brood unless a genuine emergency arises. Fortune's Folly then divides responsibility for warning its allies about Unity, preparing for diplomacy, and pursuing dungeons. Fortune's possible influence through Arlo and Grotto's altered soul-link remains unresolved.

Arlo and Grotto invite a highly capable Littan military party into the Pocket Delve to assess them before formal talks. Grotto designates the domain as an Expansion Delve and monitors how it converts mana, deaths, equipment, and combat information into resources. The visitors include a dimensional mage, a tank, a healer, an airborne weapon specialist, and her hidden mimic twin.

The party survives Grotto's maze and ambushes but is badly depleted against a Grade 20 titan. By tunneling through the arena wall, the visitors exploit the closet's looping spatial boundary and reach Arlo's private hot spring, where System rules grant them a recovery period. They return with a coordinated plan and force Grotto's minion to retreat.

Their final route leads to an impossible dimensional plant overrunning the obelisk chamber. The visiting mage invokes a goddess, who offers Arlo a choice. Arlo accepts terms that let the goddess tame the plant while preserving the visitors' earned rewards. Grotto grants all five escalated Delver status and a platinum-level reward distribution. The visitors depart through the restored portal, and Arlo receives strong Expansion Delve marks plus substantial Dungeoneering and Diplomacy progress. His Pocket Delve has now demonstrated sovereign authority and attracted direct divine notice.

Arlo and Grotto use their soul connection to reforge Arlo's abilities around dependable attacks, sustained mana use, protective auras, forced movement, and spell redirection. Meanwhile, word arrives that Hiward's king and major political figures intend to visit. Arlo and Grotto rapidly remodel the Pocket Delve into a diplomatic estate.

Varrin brings political and etiquette advisers, including his younger sister, while a dreamforger upgrades Arlo's throwing hammer. After intensive instruction, Arlo begins accepting the presentation of his domain as independent territory. An Eschendur Triarch arrives early and offers formal recognition and possible treaties if Arlo establishes a government for the dimensional space.

Arlo then opens a checkpoint for the Hiwardian delegation. The Kingsguard inspects the estate and rates Arlo and his party as major threats, while acknowledging that the domain's hidden geometry makes precise assessment difficult. Arlo agrees to limits on portals and room changes during the visit and returns a recovered sword to the head of the Kingsguard. Hiward's king, a first-generation platinum Delver, enters under the negotiated security arrangement. The royal gathering begins with Arlo's unknown origin, unusual advancement, and connections to Fortune and Orexis still matters of official concern.

Hiward's king explains that the realm wants Fortune's Folly alive, advancing, and sharing intelligence on avatar threats. He warns that Littan recruitment could create divided loyalties for Varrin. During the gathering, Grotto detects suspicious movement by a servant. Central investigators find a concealed teleport weave behind Arlo's wardrobe, powered slowly enough to avoid easy detection.

A Hiwardian lord then publicly attacks Arlo's credibility, revealing his lack of records before his first Delve. Arlo admits that he was reincarnated from another universe and defends Etja as Orexis's victim rather than an ally. The confrontation proves to be a distraction. Grotto discovers that the king, Fortune's Folly, Varrin's sister, and the Eschendur delegation have vanished from a guarded lounge.

Ealdric exposes the apparent Kingsguard detail as impostors and kills them. The lounge is a teleportation array with several lethal possible destinations. Ealdric and two powerful allies pursue the abductors before the array is destroyed. Arlo evacuates the remaining guests and subdues the accusing lord alive when he attacks in an apparently compromised state. The false Lord Director escapes through the bedroom weave. Unable to locate his allies across planes, Arlo prepares to follow the same route despite knowing it may be a trap.

Fortune and Avarice warn Arlo against entering the hostile portal, but he refuses to abandon companions he can still sense alive. He trades with Avarice for deific protection against mental effects, tools that reveal divine illusion, and an extra mental focus, accepting a future retrieval obligation in return.

After escaping a teleport loop, Arlo meets Hysteria, the avatar behind the abduction. Hysteria has trapped the captives in a false lounge and intends to steal the identities of influential people. A five-person force defeats Arlo, but his deific protection keeps him free of domination. He and Grotto find a weakness in their restraint, break the illusion, distribute protection, and invite the captives into Arlo's party so the escape card can carry them all. Varrin's sister remains controlled and cannot immediately accept.

Arlo invokes the Dread Star. Its attack reduces Hysteria's body to a stain and forces the final party invitation through. As the prison hurtles toward the world, Central extracts the group with the escape card. They reach a western desert and retreat into Arlo's closet before the impact destroys nearby mountains. Hysteria survives as a skeleton, follows through the closing portal, and begins rebuilding inside the Pocket Delve.

Hysteria calls a temporary intermission inside Arlo's closet, then demonstrates that ordinary physical and soul attacks cannot damage the avatar's skeleton. Hysteria kills three Eschendur delegates through domination and tries to seize the Triarch. Nuralie extracts the ruler while Etja combines several spells into Incorporate, consuming Hysteria's disguise and part of the avatar's manifested essence. The act leaves Hysteria weakened but makes Etja dangerously focused on consuming more.

A five-person Wasteland force attacks the mansion. Its paladin supports the group with healing, consecration, and blood magic while a martial fighter, Runeweaver, elemental caster, and hidden archer divide the party. Varrin joins the fight in improved Ravvenblaq armor. Arlo kills the elemental caster and Runeweaver, but the paladin restores them by sacrificing its own flesh. Arlo redirects a massive fire beam back onto the caster, then later detonates the edge of the mansion, apparently killing the Runeweaver and paladin.

The victory exposes a worse crisis. Grotto has suffered grave damage, the portal barrier is down, and Etja lies unconscious near the obelisk. An apparent Wasteland archer is interfering with the Delve's central systems. Arlo, Xim, and Varrin turn from the ruined mansion toward rescuing Grotto and securing the obelisk.

Arlo reaches Grotto's sealed control room through the fourth dimension. Grotto's organic body is disabled and pinned by an arrow, but his Core remains alive. Emergency System access reveals that Hysteria used the Wasteland archer as a disguise, disabled Grotto, and attached a device to the obelisk. The device projects a vastly stronger commander surrounded by unstable souls. He detects Arlo's observation and nearly kills Arlo, Xim, and Varrin from afar before they confront Hysteria directly.

Hysteria dominates much of the party, but Etja resists an order to harm Xim. Avarice then arrives with an anti-spiritual golem, ends the domination, and imprisons Hysteria. The Wasteland paladin resumes a blood sacrifice until Nuralie kills him. His failed ritual creates a powerful blood-born icon that traps and drains the party.

Arlo grants temporary control of the Pocket Delve to its administrator. Restored systems and golems help drive the icon into Dominion Ivy, which consumes it. Grotto's Core is installed in the obelisk with an estimated three-hour repair. Arlo detains the surviving pugilist pending an investigation into possible control and declares the Pocket Delve provisional sovereign neutral territory called Closetland. He must return the delegates and meet the Littan Empress in sixteen hours.
